items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Then the next thing that comes was Gerry Mulligan’s concert jazz band.

ctx.x: Thanks to Bill Harris. Bill said, “Kai is going to do a record,” he says, “sit down and write an original piece of music.” And I did and it was the first original piece — not the first original piece, I shouldn’t say, I did some in the service, but I didn’t do a whole lot of original pieces. But I wrote this piece called, I named it “Nutcracker.” And I only named it “Nutcracker” — I don’t know what made me name it “Nutcracker.” Because Connecticut is the Nutmeg State I think, isn’t it? I think Connecticut is the…

School of Music.” I don’t know if he said Manhattan, but that’s where he was going anyways. And he went back I think to school in September and left, and this trombone player, a very good trombone player from Cincinnati came on and took his place called Ola Hanson. And no he’s from Columbus. And it was while Ola was on the band that I left the group to settle in New York. It was in February of ’58. I came in for the second semester of school because I was on the verge. I’m a depression baby you know, so I was…
That must have been an experience.
